primary_meaning: Sacred rest in God: the Sabbath most commonly symbolizes participation in God’s completed work and gracious rest, understood in much Christian interpretation as fulfilled in Christ and as anticipating final, eternal rest.
primary_basis: Genesis 2:2–3 — God rests on the seventh day and blesses and sanctifies it.
Exodus 20:8–11 — Sabbath rest is grounded in God’s rest after creation.
Deuteronomy 5:12–15 — Sabbath also commemorates liberation from slavery.
Matthew 11:28–30 — Jesus offers rest to the weary, often connected theologically with Sabbath fulfillment.
Mark 2:27–28 — the Sabbath is made for humanity, and the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.
Colossians 2:16–17 — Sabbaths are described as a shadow whose substance belongs to Christ.
Hebrews 3:7–4:11 — Israel’s promised rest, God’s seventh-day rest, and the remaining “Sabbath rest” are joined typologically and eschatologically.
Revelation 14:13 — the blessed dead rest from their labors, supporting the theme of final rest.

alternatives.meaning: A continuing covenant sign and literal seventh-day sacred observance, rather than primarily a symbol superseded or transferred in Christ.
The Christian Lord’s Day—Sunday—as the transformed Sabbath, symbolizing Christ’s resurrection, new creation, and Christian worship.
Liberation from bondage and the social justice of restorative rest for servants, foreigners, animals, and the land.
Sanctification and covenant identity: Sabbath signifies that God sets apart and makes his people holy.
A prophetic pattern of a future millennial “seventh age” of history following six ages or six thousand years.

notes: There is broad consensus around sacred or divine rest as the central symbolism. There is no comparable consensus about whether that rest chiefly denotes present salvation in Christ, final heavenly rest, the weekly practice itself, Sunday observance, or a future millennium.
